description:
Kindness Music | A 1.5 hour bansuri practice for a gentler morning.

If you've been running on autopilot — jaw clenched, shoulders at your ears before the day has even begun — this is a place to start over. Soft bansuri flute. No rush. Begin with kindness. Toward yourself first.

▸ What you'll hear
• Slow bansuri flute, played softly
• A calm morning arc that opens gently, settles deep, returns soft
• 1.5 hours of seamless music — no abrupt transitions
• Played at a tempo that lets you actually breathe

▸ Best for
• Slow mornings before the world starts asking things of you
• A loving-kindness or self-compassion meditation
• Morning journaling, gentle yoga, or quiet tea
• Background for therapy or inner work
• Anyone who's been hard on themselves lately

▸ Chapters
0:00 — Begin with kindness
15:00 — Softening the morning
30:00 — Inner stillness
45:00 — Heart space
1:00:00 — Gentle return
1:15:00 — Close with care

▸ About Raga Focus
Slow Indian instrumental music for body regulation, calm cognition, and gentler mornings. New session every weekday.

Subscribe if this gave you a moment.

thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, pastoral forest-grove variant (NOT royal-palace setting). Ornate floral border in deep forest-green + gold + pink. Central figure: a serene woman in cream-and-soft-blue sari with gold thread embroidery and gold-trimmed dupatta veil over her head, seated on the ground, eyes softly closed, slight peaceful smile, holding a golden bamboo bansuri flute to her lips. Behind her: a quiet woodland grove with soft trees, dappled morning light, scattered wildflowers in the foreground, hint of a path winding into distance. Cream/aged-parchment background on the right side gives clean space for text. Overlay text 'BE KIND' in DARK FOREST-GREEN serif, large block letters, mobile-readable (scans under 1 second). Text on right, figure on left — survives YT player overlays on mobile. Soft warm luminous morning atmosphere, devotional/contemplative tone (NOT royal/grand). Vrindavan-grove aesthetic (Krishna-flute mythology) — culturally authentic anchor for Bansuri.
suno_prompt_A: Gentle Indian classical instrumental, Raga Bhupali — joyful pentatonic warm and intimate, the warm feeling of inner kindness on a fresh morning, soft bamboo bansuri flute with breathy warm tone played slowly, no tabla (Bansuri solo with drone only), soft tanpura drone in background, 432Hz, 70 BPM, warm mid-register, fresh morning melodious production, like sunlight filtering through trees in a quiet grove, hopeful and tender, seamless loop-friendly texture, no vocals, no humming, no human voice
suno_prompt_B: Instrumental only no vocals no humming, soft Indian bamboo flute bansuri solo, Raga Bhupali pentatonic warm joyful, breathy tender tone, 432Hz, 70 BPM, gentle morning warmth, soft tanpura drone backdrop, no tabla no percussion, peaceful intimate atmosphere like morning light in a forest grove, seamless loop

production_spec.loop_structure: 3 source clips (~3min each) trimmed to energetic-edges, merged with 2.5s qsin equal-power crossfades into 8:09 base unit (v5). Looped 12x with 3s qsin crossfades at loop joins. First cycle uses full v5 (preserves File 1 soft fade-in opener). Subsequent cycles use trimmed v5 (edges cut to avoid melodic-overlap on loop joins — the lesson from this session). Final 10s afade-out to silence.
production_spec.render: MP4 1920x1080 H.264 ultrafast/CRF22, AAC 192kbps stereo 48kHz, 312MB output, +faststart
production_spec.notes: MUSIC-QUALITY CARE: deliberate attention to opening 3 minutes (long Bansuri alaap intro before any energy build) — addresses the recent Sitar-cluster 2% retention cliff finding (recent Sitar ships lost 7-11pp more audience at 2:00 mark than May-era equivalents in same lanes; isolated music-quality issue in opening passages). Bhupali = joyful pentatonic but used in WARM/TENDER register here (not bright/uplifting) — fits compassion/kindness emotional intent. No tabla (Bansuri solo + tanpura drone only) — keeps the meditative/intimate space. 70 BPM = slow enough for breath, not so slow it loses momentum.
